sentence: It's important to ___ that not all information online is reliable.
explanation: To "bear in mind" significa recordar o tener en cuenta algo.
tip: Collocation with <bear>: tener en cuenta (3 words)

sentence: The new policy will ___ on the economy.
explanation: To "have a profound impact" significa tener un efecto muy grande o intenso.
tip: Collocation: have + adj. meaning 'profundo' + impact (4 words)

sentence: She managed to ___ between her career and family life.
explanation: To "strike a balance" significa encontrar un equilibrio satisfactorio entre dos extremos.
tip: Collocation with <strike>: encontrar un equilibrio (3 words)

sentence: His arguments ___, despite initial skepticism.
explanation: Si un argumento o afirmación "holds water", es válido y sólido.
tip: Idiom with <hold>: ser válido/sólido — like a container that doesn't leak (2 words)

sentence: The new evidence ___ the mysterious disappearance.
explanation: To "shed light on" algo significa ayudar a explicarlo.
tip: Idiom with <shed>: ayudar a explicar algo (3 words)

sentence: We need to ___ before the system goes live.
explanation: To "iron out the kinks" significa resolver problemas o dificultades menores.
tip: Idiom with <iron>: resolver problemas menores — like straightening wrinkles (4 words)

sentence: The decision was made ___.
explanation: Hacer algo "at the eleventh hour" significa hacerlo en el último momento posible.
tip: Idiom: en el último momento — 'at the ___ hour' (number before 12) (4 words)

sentence: He tends to ___ and make decisions too quickly.
explanation: To "jump the gun" significa actuar demasiado pronto o antes de tiempo.
tip: Idiom with <jump>: actuar antes de tiempo — like a runner starting before the signal (3 words)

sentence: The new manager is determined to ___ and improve team morale.
explanation: To "turn over a new leaf" significa empezar de nuevo y cambiar de comportamiento para mejor.
tip: Idiom with <turn>: empezar de nuevo — like flipping to a blank page (5 words)

sentence: The company is ___ a major breakthrough.
explanation: Estar "on the cusp of" algo significa estar en el punto en que algo está a punto de suceder.
tip: Idiom: a punto de — 'on the ___ of' (cusp = borde/punto) (4 words)

sentence: His explanation didn't ___ to me.
explanation: Si algo "rings true", parece ser verdadero o genuino.
tip: Idiom with <ring>: sonar verdadero/creíble (2 words)

sentence: She has a tendency to ___.
correct: make a mountain out of a molehill
explanation: To "make a mountain out of a molehill" significa exagerar la importancia de un problema pequeño.
tip: Idiom with <make>: exagerar un problema pequeño — mountain vs. molehill (7 words)

sentence: The project was a success, ___.
explanation: "By and large" significa generalmente o en su mayor parte.
tip: Idiom meaning 'en general' — ___ and ___ (3 words, nautical origin)

sentence: He decided to ___ and start his own business.
explanation: To "take the plunge" significa decidirse a hacer algo importante o difícil que llevas mucho tiempo pensando hacer.
tip: Idiom with <take>: lanzarse/decidirse — like diving into water (3 words)

sentence: The new regulations will ___ for all competitors.
explanation: To "level the playing field" significa hacer que una situación sea justa para todos.
tip: Idiom with <level>: igualar las condiciones — sports metaphor (4 words)

sentence: She's always been able to ___.
explanation: To "read between the lines" significa entender el verdadero significado de algo, aunque no se exprese directamente.
tip: Idiom with <read>: entender lo no dicho — lo que está entre las líneas (4 words)

sentence: The company is trying to ___ after a series of setbacks.
explanation: To "get your act together" significa organizarte a ti mismo y tus asuntos para poder lograr algo.
tip: Idiom with <get>: organizarse — como un actor que prepara su acto (4 words)

sentence: His comments were ___.
explanation: A "breath of fresh air" es algo nuevo y refrescante que mejora una situación.
tip: Idiom: algo refrescante y nuevo — 'a ___ of fresh air' (5 words)

sentence: We need to ___ before it becomes a bigger problem.
explanation: To "nip something in the bud" significa detener un problema en una etapa temprana antes de que empeore.
tip: Idiom with <nip>: cortar un problema de raíz — like cutting a plant bud (5 words)

sentence: The company decided to ___ to the minor infractions.
explanation: To "turn a blind eye" significa ignorar deliberadamente algo que sabes que está mal.
tip: Idiom with <turn>: hacer la vista gorda — 'turn a ___ eye' (4 words)
